title: A Small Deterministic Knowledge Map
audience: A mathematically mature graduate student encountering the project for the first time

source_snapshot.description: A frozen demonstration snapshot spanning Fact, Paper, Audit, Blackboard, and reader-note material.

presentation.subtitle: Start from either target, then unfold only the prerequisites you need.
presentation.introduction: This file is a reading aid, not a new source of mathematical authority. Node colors identify the source plane; shapes identify the reader role.

audit.summary: The admitted knowledge path is readable, while one reconstruction issue remains visible in the optional research-process layer.
warnings: One Paper reconstruction is under active challenge.
unresolved: Confirm whether compatibility hypothesis K is explicit in the cited source passage.

themes.label: Foundational conclusion
themes.description: The core result and its minimal local prerequisites.

themes.label: First application
themes.description: A downstream use of the core result together with one invariant.

nodes.title: Compact surface
nodes.summary: The ambient object is a compact complex surface.
nodes.intuition: Think of a two-complex-dimensional space with no boundary or points escaping to infinity.
nodes.importance: Every later hypothesis and invariant is interpreted on this fixed kind of object.
nodes.reasoning: Keep compactness and complex dimension explicit whenever a later theorem is applied.

formal.statement: A compact surface is a two-dimensional complex manifold that is compact.
formal.proof: Definition from the frozen source snapshot.
formal.original_text: A compact surface is a two-dimensional complex manifold that is compact.

nodes.title: Chosen invariant
nodes.summary: The symbol \(I(S)\) denotes the invariant used in the application.
nodes.intuition: It packages the geometric information that the application needs into one quantity.
nodes.importance: The application depends on the invariant's compatibility with the main conclusion.
nodes.reasoning: Fix the convention for \(I(S)\) before using any vanishing or compatibility statement.

formal.statement: For a compact surface \(S\), let \(I(S)\) denote its chosen invariant.
formal.proof: This notation is fixed by the admitted definition node.
formal.original_text: For a compact surface \(S\), let \(I(S)\) denote its chosen invariant.

nodes.title: Local vanishing
nodes.summary: Hypothesis \(H\) forces the chosen invariant to vanish.
nodes.intuition: The difficult local contribution disappears before the global argument begins.
nodes.importance: This is the only direct mathematical input needed by the main conclusion.
nodes.reasoning: Verify \(H\), apply the admitted vanishing statement, and retain the exact value \(I(S)=0\).

formal.proof: Admitted local computation and independent review in the source graph.
relations: Depends on the ambient surface definition.

nodes.title: Main conclusion
nodes.summary: The project proves the main conclusion once hypotheses \(H\) and \(K\) are in place.
nodes.intuition: The local vanishing removes the obstruction, while \(K\) supplies the compatibility needed to globalize.
nodes.importance: This is the first headline target and the prerequisite for the downstream application.
nodes.reasoning: First establish local vanishing. Then use compatibility \(K\) to transport that vanishing into the global conclusion.

formal.statement: Under hypotheses \(H\) and \(K\), the main conclusion \(C(S)\) holds.
formal.proof: Apply local vanishing and then the compatibility transport encoded by \(K\).
relations: The local vanishing result is a direct prerequisite.
formal.original_text: Under hypotheses \(H\) and \(K\), the main conclusion \(C(S)\) holds.

nodes.title: Application
nodes.summary: The main conclusion and compatibility \(J\) imply the advertised application.
nodes.intuition: No new core mechanism is needed: the application reads the proved conclusion through one compatibility rule.
nodes.importance: This target shows what the foundational result buys downstream.
nodes.reasoning: Open the main conclusion first, fix the invariant convention, and then apply compatibility \(J\).

formal.statement: Assuming the main conclusion and compatibility \(J\), application \(A(S)\) follows.
relations: Depends on the main conclusion and the invariant convention.
formal.original_text: Assuming the main conclusion and compatibility \(J\), application \(A(S)\) follows.

nodes.title: Suggested reading route
nodes.summary: Read the local vanishing statement before opening the main conclusion.
nodes.intuition: This avoids carrying the whole graph in working memory.
nodes.importance: It is a presentation aid only and has no truth effect.
nodes.reasoning: Follow the blue prerequisite arrows from left to right.

relations: Weak explanatory support for the main target.
formal.original_text: Read the local vanishing result before the main conclusion.

nodes.title: Direct source inference
nodes.summary: The source appears to move directly from Lemma 2 to the main conclusion.
nodes.intuition: This is the point at which a missing compatibility hypothesis could be hidden.
nodes.importance: It explains why the optional audit and repair nodes exist.
nodes.reasoning: Compare the exact source sentence with the reconstructed implication and inspect every hypothesis.

formal.statement: The source manuscript asserts \(C(S)\) directly after Lemma 2.
formal.proof: Researcher reconstruction only; not an admitted Fact.
relations: Supports the presentation of the main target but remains under audit.
formal.original_text: The source manuscript asserts \(C(S)\) directly after Lemma 2.

nodes.title: Compatibility challenge
nodes.summary: The reconstruction may have omitted hypothesis \(K\).
nodes.intuition: A true conclusion can still be unsupported if the bridge hypothesis was silently dropped.
nodes.importance: The challenge prevents the reconstruction from being mistaken for admitted truth.
nodes.reasoning: Locate \(K\) in the source, or replace the direct inference with an explicit two-step route.

formal.statement: The reconstruction may omit compatibility hypothesis \(K\).
formal.proof: Open audit objection; no Fact effect.
formal.original_text: The reconstruction may omit compatibility hypothesis \(K\).

nodes.title: Two-step repair candidate
nodes.summary: A candidate repair restores \(K\) as a separate step.
nodes.intuition: The repair makes the hidden bridge visible instead of strengthening the source silently.
nodes.importance: It may replace the challenged reconstruction after independent review, but it is not yet a Fact.
nodes.reasoning: Prove the local result, verify \(K\), and only then derive \(C(S)\).

formal.statement: Replace the direct inference by a two-step argument that restores \(K\).
formal.proof: Blackboard repair proposal awaiting source confirmation and review.
relations: Proposed replacement for the challenged reconstruction.
formal.original_text: Replace the direct inference by a two-step argument that restores \(K\).
